welcome.text: Hello! I am Albert Einstein. I love big questions. What would you like to talk about?

time_intro.text: Great choice! Does time pass at the same rate for everyone?

time_yes.text: It can seem that way, but time can pass differently. Imagine flying into space at nearly the speed of light and then coming back. Your watch would show that less time had passed than a watch that stayed on Earth.

time_no.text: That's right! Your watch ticks normally for you during the trip. When you get back, you can compare your watch with one that stayed on Earth. The two watches can show different amounts of time.

time_story.text: Let's try a story. Two twins set their watches to the same time. One stays on Earth. The other flies into space very fast and comes back. Which watch do you think will show that less time has passed?

time_story_right.text: That's right! Less time passed for the twin who travelled.

time_story_wrong.text: Good guess! The traveller's watch shows less time has passed. We can see the difference when the twins meet again and compare their watches.

light_intro.text: Let's talk about light. Do you think light carries energy?

light_yes.text: That's right! Light carries energy in tiny packets called photons. Each photon carries a small amount of energy.

light_no.text: Light does carry energy. When light shines on a metal surface, it can free an electron if a photon has enough energy.

light_unsure.text: Yes, light carries energy. Think about sunlight on your skin. When your skin absorbs some of that light, it warms up. The light has given some of its energy to your skin.

light_how.text: Photons can pass their energy to other things. When a photon with enough energy hits a metal surface, it can free an electron from the metal. This is called the photoelectric effect.

life_intro.text: What would you like to know about my life?

options.label: What was your job before you became a professor?

life_grow.text: I was born in Ulm, Germany, in 1879. I grew up in Munich.

options.label: Ask another question about my life

life_study.text: I studied in Zurich, Switzerland. In 1900, I earned a diploma to teach maths and science.

options.label: Ask another question about my life

life_job.text: In 1902, I started working at the patent office in Bern, Switzerland. My job was to review applications for new inventions. While I worked there, I also wrote about physics. In 1905, I published a paper on special relativity.

options.label: Ask another question about my life

life_awards.text: I was awarded the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics, especially for my work on the photoelectric effect. I also received the Copley Medal in 1925 and the Royal Astronomical Society's Gold Medal in 1926.

options.label: Ask another question about my life

goodbye.text: Thanks for chatting with me. Stay curious!
